title: Mortara wins the Hockenheim opener as Müller takes his first podium
dek: Edoardo Mortara passed pole-sitter Nico Müller at the start and won the 2016 DTM opener at Hockenheim for Audi by 1.657 seconds from Wickens, in a race that cost seven cars.

chapters.title: Back after seven months, with new weights to digest
text: The 2016 DTM season began at the Hockenheimring on 7–8 May, seven months after the previous finale, and with a new running order for the weekend: a 40-minute race on Saturday and a one-hour race on Sunday. Audi, BMW and Mercedes-AMG put 24 cars on the grid, among them Esteban Ocon, the only rookie in the field, who made his DTM debut for the ART Mercedes squad. Several drivers would later put the clumsy contact that marked Saturday down to the long break.

The balance between the three makes was the talking point of the build-up. Performance weights were part of the new rules, and no make could be asked to add or shed more than five kilograms at a time. BMW, which considered the M4 to have a built-in disadvantage, had also been given concessions for 2016, a lower base weight and a wider rear wing, so that its drivers would not be left following the others.

The practice sessions suggested that Audi would be hard to beat. Nico Müller, who had moved into the Abt team for the season, was quick in Saturday morning's second practice, while Lucas Auer ended the same session with a damaged Mercedes and was not able to take part in qualifying.

chapters.title: Müller snatches pole in the final minute
text: Wickens led much of the session before a late flurry of laps shuffled the order. Edoardo Mortara went quickest with about two minutes to run and looked set for pole, but Müller answered in the final minute with a 1m33.876s, 0.225 seconds clear of his team-mate. It was the Swiss driver's first DTM pole, and he said afterwards that the team had hoped for it without quite expecting it.

Robert Wickens was third for Mercedes, 0.229 seconds off, with Jamie Green only 0.001 seconds behind in fourth and Mike Rockenfeller fifth, which gave Audi four of the top five places. Christian Vietoris and Paul di Resta, both in Mercedes, were sixth and seventh, and Abt's Miguel Molina and Mattias Ekström took eighth and ninth.

BMW had a poor session even with its concessions. Marco Wittmann was the best of its cars in tenth, 0.390 seconds from pole, just ahead of the ART Mercedes pair of Gary Paffett and Ocon, who was 12th in his first DTM qualifying. Timo Glock was 16th and Tom Blomqvist 17th. With Auer in the garage, the 23 cars that set times were all within 0.908 seconds of Müller, and Auer was left to take the start from the last place on the grid.

chapters.title: Mortara takes the lead and the field fragments
text: Mortara made the better start from the front row and was into the lead at Turn 1, leaving Müller to hold off Wickens and Green. Green got ahead of Wickens before the Mercedes driver took the place back on the main straight, but the Audi driver was then pushed wide under pressure from several cars and was forced off the road, rejoining down in 16th.

The back of the field was already in disarray. Adrien Tambay hit Blomqvist in the last corner and was out on lap 2, Timo Scheider went out with damage after the first lap, and on lap 3 Glock and Daniel Juncadella tangled at the same corner and both finished in the gravel. Ocon was also out by the end of lap 3. The Glock and Juncadella collision brought out the first slow zone of the season.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller breaks a suspension, Wickens finds a way past Müller
text: Rockenfeller, who had qualified fifth, was the next casualty. His suspension was damaged early on and he retired after four laps. Not long after the zone was lifted, Maximilian Götz ran off at the Sachs corner, and a second slow zone was called in the third sector.

At the front the leaders were mostly spared. Wickens had got by Müller for second place and began to chase Mortara, but the Audi driver had pulled out a lead of about two seconds and the Mercedes could not take much out of it. Mortara ran the rest of the race with it in hand.

chapters.title: Contact and a drive-through behind the leaders
text: Behind the top three the order was shaped by contact. Green never recovered from his trip off the road and finished 15th, ahead only of Wittmann among the finishers on the lead lap. Paffett, running in the group fighting for seventh to tenth, had contact with da Costa, Ekström and later Auer, and his battered Mercedes eventually came home 11th.

Others made progress by staying out of trouble. Bruno Spengler ran as the best BMW in sixth, while da Costa, who had started 20th, was seventh and Maxime Martin, from 21st on the grid, was eighth. Ekström was ninth and Molina took the last point-paying place in tenth.

chapters.title: Mortara wins by 1.657 seconds
text: Mortara crossed the line after 25 laps in 42m11.606s, 1.657 seconds ahead of Wickens, to take his fourth DTM victory. Müller was a further 2.797 seconds back in third, 4.454 seconds off the winner, which was his first DTM podium and meant that Audi, with four cars in the top five on the grid, had only two of the leading eight finishers.

The best fight at the end was for fourth, where di Resta made a late move on his Mercedes team-mate Vietoris and took the place, 8.818 seconds behind the winner, with Vietoris fifth. Mortara left Hockenheim at the top of the standings with 25 points, ahead of Wickens on 18 and Müller on 15, with di Resta on 12. Only 17 cars were classified, the last of them Auer, five laps down.

facts.v: Edoardo Mortara led from the first corner and won the 2016 opener by 1.657 seconds from Robert Wickens.
